subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA qualification — Elara Health

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode & HIPAA qualification — Elara Health

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

1) Goal: Evaluate which deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC) meets Elara Health's HIPAA, audit, and data residency needs.
2) Ask from your side: confirmation of SOC 2 report, BAA process, encryption and audit log capabilities, and recommended architecture for PHI workloads.

High-level guidance from our side: 
- Hosted API: fastest to integrate, supports encrypted-in-transit and at-rest options for managed storage. For PHI workflows we generally recommend Dedicated or Private due to isolation and contractual controls, unless you accept a strict BAA + additional controls and restricted routing.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, isolated compute, customer-scoped quotas and improved tenancy guarantees — good middle ground for production PHI when you want predictable throughput without managing infra.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and air-gapped options — strongest standing for regulated audits and tight control over logs/retention.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll share our SOC 2 report and a BAA template for your legal/security review (attached).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (Dylan) to go through network, KMS, and audit-log specifics. Can you share 2x windows next week that work for you?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf, redwood-baa-template.docx, deployment-options-onepager.pdf

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@elarahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Elara Health Security Team <security@elarahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA qualification — Elara Health

Thanks for the recap, Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from my security team: 

- Can you confirm that Redwood's SOC 2 report covers the Hosted API and Dedicated offerings, or is it scoped only to the control plane? We need to show auditors which deployment modes are covered.
- For encryption at rest: do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in Dedicated and Private? If so, which KMS providers are supported?
- Audit logs and retention: we need immutable audit logs (access, admin actions, model version rollouts) with retention options up to 7 years; does Redwood provide this and can logs be exported to our S3?
- BAA: is the BAA a standard template or do you accept countered redlines? Our legal will likely redline a few clauses.

We'd like the SOC 2 and BAA to review before the technical call. Once we have that, I'll propose times for the deep-dive (security + platform engineers).

Best,
Sara
Director of Engineering, Security
Elara Health
sara.khan@elarahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA qualification — Elara Health

Sara — thanks, noted. Attaching our latest SOC 2 report and a BAA template for review (see attachments). Short answers to your bullets below, and we can cover the details in the call: 

- SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II (2025) report covers the hosted Redwood platform (control plane) and the Dedicated offering for inference serving — it documents controls for access, change management, and monitoring. Private/on-prem deployments are not covered by Redwood's hosted SOC but we provide an evidence pack and customer-run controls guidance for on-prem installs.

- Customer-managed keys: Supported for Dedicated and Private. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault integrations for CMK; Private on-prem can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11 compatible).

- Audit logs & retention: We emit admin and access audit logs (model deployments, admin actions, API keys usage). For Dedicated and Private you can configure log export to your S3/Cloud Storage or to a SIEM via our event streaming (Kafka/Splunk). Retention policies are configurable; for Dedicated we can guarantee export/retention SLAs via contract to support multi-year retention.

- BAA process: We provide a standard BAA template; customers commonly counter with specific liability and termination clauses. We can accept redlines via DocuSign.

Proposed technical deep-dive scope (Dylan will lead): network/VPC peering, KMS integration and key rotation, audit log exports and retention, data residency options, and performance/latency implications of Dedicated vs Private. 

Dylan — are you available Wed 18th or Thu 19th for a 60-minute session? Sara, if you can give 2x windows (30-60min) we’ll lock the invite.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf, redwood-baa-template.docx, deployment-options-onepager.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
